beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a secrets manager at runtime; never hard-code or commit the URI/keys into the repo or tests. Provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.

Use a least-privilege database user for each logical component (eg: readonly user for GP/specialist/pharmacy agents and a write-capable user only for the orchestrator) rather than using the account master key for all operations.

Keep PHI out of logs and avoid printing the connection string or patient data to stdout; enable encryption in transit (TLS) and rely on the provider's at-rest encryption (do not log unencrypted documents).

Choose the collection/partition key to be patient_id (or another high-cardinality patient identifier) when creating each collection so queries for a single patient's records hit a single partition and remain efficient and cost-predictable.

Create single-field indexes on any field used as a lookup key in queries (e.g., patient_id, referral.patient_id, medication.patient_id) and create compound indexes when queries filter/sort on multiple fields together; create indexes idempotently in the seed script (create_index / createIndex).

When storing embeddings for vector search, store them as a dedicated numeric array field (e.g., embedding: [f1, f2, ...]) and keep semantic metadata in separate fields; ensure the embedding dimensionality is recorded in documents or index metadata.

Provision any vector index explicitly with the cluster's vector indexing options (method: hnsw/ivf/diskann, metric: cosine/l2) matching your embedding dimensionality and recall/latency budget instead of relying on default B-tree indexes for embedding arrays.
Use connection pooling and tune maxPoolSize/minPoolSize in the MongoDB driver connection options appropriate to app concurrency (pymongo: maxPoolSize) to avoid frequent connect/disconnect overhead.
Enable and rely on retryable writes/reads and implement exponential backoff for transient network/503 errors; wrap critical operations in a retry loop with limited attempts and jitter.

Set an appropriate writeConcern/readConcern (or equivalent) for operations that must be durable/consistent (for example, w=majority for writes that must be persisted before continuing) and use lower w when lower latency is acceptable.

Use explain() and the provider's profiler or MCP tools to verify that queries are using the intended indexes and to measure RU / cost of queries before shipping; add tests that assert explain plan uses index where performance matters.

Avoid large skip() pagination for patient timelines; prefer range-based pagination (use a timestamp or an indexed sequence field and query with $lt/$gt + limit) to keep queries efficient across partitions.

Make the seed script idempotent: create collections and indexes if missing (createCollection/create_index with if-not-exists semantics or ignore duplicate-key/index-exists errors) and use upsert (update_one(..., upsert=True)) for fixtures.

Provision throughput appropriately for collections (manual RU/s or autoscale) to match expected read/write patterns; for bursty or variable workloads prefer autoscale to avoid RU throttling of the orchestrator or agents.

Use a separate database or collection for tests (or mock the DB) and avoid running tests against production data; clear or tear down test documents after tests, and mock LLM/embedding calls in unit tests.

Include a schema_version attribute in documents and design upgrade/migration paths (transform scripts or new fields handled by application code) so orchestrator/agents can evolve without breaking older records.

Use multi-document transactions only when necessary for atomic cross-document updates, and otherwise design operations to be idempotent; verify that transactions are supported for your Mongo wire version on the managed cluster before relying on them.
Monitor RUs (or the provider metric equivalent), connection count, index sizes and slow queries; alert on RU throttling, frequent 429s or elevated tail latency so you can tune indexes or throughput.

For patient-sensitive fields, consider client-side field-level encryption (CSFLE) for HIPAA-sensitive attributes if the platform and Mongo API version support it; otherwise minimize risk by encrypting fields before writing from the application layer.

When using embeddings/LLM synthesis, record provenance metadata (model, prompt, timestamp, embedding model version) alongside generated care plans and treat generated care plans as auditable documents written to a dedicated careplans collection with patient_id partitioning.
